analysis.title: GOAL: Asset Allocation - Giving credit to balance (October 2026)
key_insights: GS stays overweight equities on both 3-month and 12-month horizons but frames the October update as more focused on balance. Within equities it is overweight MSCI Asia Pac ex Japan, TOPIX and the S&P 500, and underweight the STOXX Europe 600.

Government bonds are neutral on a 3-month view and overweight on a 12-month view. The US, Germany and UK are preferred and Japan is underweight. The firm's recent GOAL title describes bonds as gradually moving from headwind to hedge.

Credit is underweight overall, with USD IG and USD HY preferred inside the bucket and EUR IG and EUR HY least preferred. Commodities are neutral overall, with precious metals the preferred sub-sector. Gold is overweight with a 12-month target of $5,235/oz against $4,038 at pricing on October 28th, 2026.
Cash is overweight on the 3-month horizon and neutral on the 12-month horizon.

Global growth and inflation have deteriorated because of the Middle East war. GS expects improvement as inflation normalises, with real growth near trend, which it says points back to a Goldilocks-like backdrop.
Earnings growth is materially outstripping nominal GDP growth, and growth momentum is expected to peak. Market measures of inflation have started to normalise but macro inflation data has not yet.

Equities can buffer higher bond yields as long as earnings growth is strong. A 10-year yield rise of more than 2 standard deviations over three months has tended to weigh on equities, so the speed of the move matters.

The GS Risk Appetite Indicator fell to -0.5 in October. Markets are pricing a more restrictive monetary policy backdrop, and hawkish rates pricing and rising long-dated real yields have started to weigh on growth sentiment. Cross-asset sentiment and positioning are back to more neutral levels.

The equity tail-risk framework still shows a less negative asymmetry, but the business cycle and sentiment signals are worsening. The risk of a stagflationary shock and of 60/40 drawdowns has moderated.

Tech sector weight in US equities is now above Tech Bubble levels, and concentration in the largest 10 stocks has risen in the US and more recently in EM benchmarks. Since June 2026, AI-related stocks have been driven more by earnings than by valuation expansion.

Hyperscaler capex is weighing on free cash flow and is expected to pressure ROE for hyperscalers and mega-cap tech. In past TMT drawdowns, real assets, low vol, high dividend yield and value stocks held up better than the S&P 500.

Equity/bond correlation turned positive after COVID, which GS links to sticky inflation and fiscal concerns pushing bond yields up. Style diversification has become more useful than regional diversification.

Realised equity dispersion is at the highest level since the early 2000s and implied correlations are close to all-time lows. The Carry Opportunity Indicator is near its lowest since the GFC, signalling poor asymmetry for carry trades and more vulnerability to growth and rate shocks.

GS proposes hedges: front-end rate receivers as medium-term recession hedges, TLT puts for tactical long-maturity bond exposure, and long-dated S&P 500 calls to add asymmetry and upside convexity. Convertibles look more attractive as equity-like bonds, and issuance has risen on AI funding needs.

Long-term section: the World Portfolio (US$289trn coverage) has shifted toward equities, especially when private markets are included. Historical optimal portfolios held more bonds and gold than the market-value World Portfolio, and adding gold or real assets improved Sharpe ratios in GS backtests since 1950.

Ten-year scenario analysis compares Goldilocks plus AI boom, Goldilocks, reflation, Goldilocks plus AI bust, stagnation and stagflation. Returns on the S&P 500 and bonds and the optimal bond weight differ widely across them.

sector_views.rationale: Tech weight exceeds Tech Bubble levels and hyperscaler capex weighs on FCF and ROE, but AI-related stocks are earnings-driven. GS shows low vol, high dividend yield and value stocks as diversifiers against TMT drawdowns.
Real assets did well during Tech-led drawdowns and offer uncorrelated real returns when inflation is high. S&P GSCI Precious Metals is preferred within commodities and gold is overweight.

sector_views.sector: Low vol and high dividend yield equities
sector_views.rationale: They can outperform the market ex Tech on a risk-adjusted basis and help diversify Tech exposure.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 earnings growth is materially outstripping US nominal GDP growth, per GS (dotted lines in the chart are GIR forecasts).
Since June 2026, AI-related US stocks have been more driven by earnings than by valuations, in contrast to other markets.
Hyperscaler capex as a percentage of operating cash flow is rising against the 2026 consensus line, which is weighing on free cash flow. ROEs for mega-cap tech are expected to decline.
S&P 500 profitability has been boosted by the TMT sector.

macro_indicators.indicator: US 10-year government bond yield, GS target
macro_indicators.interpretation: The path of falling yields supports the 12-month overweight in US government bonds, with a 10.1% total return forecast.
GS forecasts a decline of 35.0% over 12 months, in line with its view that Middle East war pressure on inflation fades.
The forecast decline is 34.1% over 12 months.
Total return forecasts are 3.6%, 7.8% and 13.5%, supporting the equity overweight.
Implies 29.6% upside over 12 months, the largest forecast gain among listed assets.

crypto_views: Crypto appears as a component in the World Portfolio asset weights chart, and Bitcoin (data from 2010) is plotted among assets outside the benchmarks on a Sharpe ratio versus correlation-with-World-Portfolio chart. The text gives no directional crypto view.

trade_ideas.description: Long 12m 25-delta receivers on 1y or 2y USD rates as a medium-term recession hedge
trade_ideas.rationale: Front-end receivers look attractive as medium-term recession hedges in simulated PnL across US recessions.

trade_ideas.description: Tactically long maturity bonds using TLT puts, with the option-price adjusted yield close to its highs
trade_ideas.rationale: The US 30y yield less the annualised price of a 3m put on 20y+ USTs (TLT) is near its highs.

trade_ideas.description: Long-dated S&P 500 calls (2-year, rolled after 1 year) plus USD 1-3y IG as an asymmetric equity exposure
trade_ideas.rationale: Long-dated equity calls can improve asymmetry or increase upside convexity.

risk_factors: Rising bond yields from sticky inflation and fiscal concerns are difficult for equities to digest, and the equity/bond correlation has been positive since COVID.
Hawkish rates pricing and rising long-dated real yields weigh on risk appetite.
Worsening business cycle and sentiment signals in the drawdown model, even though the overall tail-risk asymmetry is less negative.
Tech concentration and valuations: Tech weight is above Tech Bubble levels and equities are again expensive on Shiller P/E.
Low risk premia leave carry trades vulnerable to growth and rate shocks.
Hyperscaler AI capex is weighing on FCF and ROE.
charts_described: Chart on page 5 plots S&P 500 earnings growth against US nominal GDP growth, with the title stating that earnings are materially outstripping nominal GDP.
Page 30 chart shows the Carry Opportunity Indicator near its lowest levels since the GFC, plotted against an inverted growth score.
Page 61 charts show realised dispersion at the highest level since the early 2000s and 3-month implied correlation near all-time lows for the S&P 500 and EURO STOXX 50.
Page 21 chart shows the TMT weight in US equities above Tech Bubble levels.
Page 23 chart decomposes returns since June 2026 for AI baskets into earnings, valuations and FX, with the title stating AI-related stocks were more earnings-driven than valuation-driven.
Page 27 chart shows the proportion of S&P 500 stocks with a negative beta has increased, similar to the Tech Bubble.
vol_and_positioning: Realised equity dispersion is at the highest level since the early 2000s, measured as the average realised vol of underlying stocks minus the realised vol of the S&P 500.
Implied correlations (3-month, 50-delta call) for the S&P 500 and EURO STOXX 50 are close to all-time lows.

Cross-asset sentiment and positioning are back to more neutral levels, using the average percentile of sentiment indicators since 2007. GS's own cross-asset positioning note from October 19 describes positioning as turning more defensive.

The Carry Opportunity Indicator (EM, sovereign and corporate credit, FX, equity volatility, yield curve) is near its lowest levels since the GFC. Credit spreads and term premia are relatively low even though all-in credit yields are elevated.

Hedging: front-end receivers (12m 25-delta on 1y or 2y USD rates) as medium-term recession hedges, TLT puts for tactical long-maturity bonds, and long-dated S&P 500 calls for upside convexity. The report also shows 3m 25-delta normalised put/call skew and cross-asset hedges for growth or stagflation shocks.
Equity long/short hedge funds can benefit from dispersion, and CTAs have often delivered stronger returns when inflation is elevated.
geopolitical: Global growth and inflation have deteriorated due to the Middle East war, per the page 3 title. GS expects improvement as inflation normalises.

tension_points.bull_case: Equities can buffer higher bond yields as long as earnings growth is strong. GS shows that S&P 500 returns held up in historical periods of high EPS growth even when 10-year yields rose.
tension_points.bear_case: Rising yields from sticky inflation and fiscal concerns are hard for equities to digest, equity/bond correlations are positive, and hawkish rates pricing is weighing on growth sentiment.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A rise in the 10-year yield of more than 2 standard deviations over three months, or EPS growth slowing, would break the buffer.

tension_points.bull_case: The equity tail-risk framework points to a less negative asymmetry, and the risk of a stagflationary shock and 60/40 drawdowns has moderated.
tension_points.bear_case: Signals from the business cycle and sentiment are worsening in the drawdown model, valuations are expensive and Tech concentration is above Tech Bubble levels.

tension_points.bull_case: Normalising inflation with real growth close to trend points to a return to a Goldilocks-like backdrop, which has historically favoured risk assets.
tension_points.bear_case: Macro inflation data has not yet normalised and a monetary policy factor that stays hawkish pushes the backdrop toward reflation or a balanced bear.

theme_stances.evidence: Equities can buffer higher bond yields as long as there is strong earnings growth
